claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements.
A deep learning potential can describe high-entropy materials in both solid and liquid states.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys generally, rather than only to the cited high-entropy carbonitrides.
The intervention is applicable at temperatures near the alloys' high melting points.
Atomic configurations and pair correlations are the structural mediators affected by the deep learning potential.
A deep learning potential will represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid better than traditional EAM references.
Better representation of liquid configurations will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference-target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Deep-learning potentials can be used to predict melting behavior and structural changes in solid and liquid high-entropy carbonitrides.
Using a deep learning potential will improve the accuracy of predicted melting temperatures relative to EAM references.
Using a deep learning potential will improve the accuracy of predicted phase transitions relative to EAM references.
The magnitude of the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is unknown and requires further investigation.
Comparison of predicted melting temperatures and phase transitions with experimental data can test the hypothesis.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental thermodynamic properties would falsify the hypothesis.
